directions.brief: Subject built on P3 Trace as subject; drawing language: typeset diagram.
Subject built on P4 Stack in depth; drawing language: orthographic elevation.
Subject built on P10 Voice field; drawing language: survey plan.
Subject built on P15 Cell field; drawing language: patent section.
Subject built on P13 Capture; drawing language: hidden-line isometric. This pattern is outside the category's column: say why this machine is the exception, or say plainly it doesn't fit.

variants.subject: One bright spectrum line, set like a textbook figure on a log-frequency axis, crisp and jagged inside the focal band and smoothed to a soft hump outside it.
controls: focus: position. The focal span (a 1.5 px bracket on the axis) and the dense, jagged stretch of the line slide together along the axis, 100 Hz to 8 kHz, about 290 px; the line re-keys where it's sharp.
tilt: rotation. The whole line turns about its point at the focus, ±18° (36° over the range; a little more than the true ±6 dB/oct slope so it clears the 30° floor).
blur: shape. Outside the band the line is smoothed by a wider kernel: at 0 the partials stand as sharp peaks right across, at 100 the line outside the band is a soft hump with no peaks.

mix: position. A dark hairline ghost of the dry, untouched spectrum sits under the bright line; mix drops it from on the line (0) to 34 px below (100), so the gap is how far the result has left the input.
variants.reference: opxy/reference/README.md (stock engine screens: the wavetable engine's single waveform) beside library/toro-blocks/contact.png for weight
risks: Easy to read as an analyser: the line is a fixed test spectrum (an effect page gets no audio), so it shows what the settings do, not what's playing. That has to be obvious or it reads as broken.

Tilt as rotation is slightly exaggerated (±18° for ±6 dB/oct) to clear the 30° floor; a 400 px line turned 18° pokes towards the header at the ends, so the pivot height and the turn need checking on the contact sheet.
Mix is the weakest channel: a ghost dropping away is a convention, not the sound. At the default (mix 100) the ghost is permanently 34 px down and adds clutter.
Budget: sharp-in-band needs dense points, so the line is three mutable outlines (left, band, right) of 31 centre points each; focus re-keys all three. Four paths is the cap.

variants.subject: Six octave bands stood up as cards in an oblique elevation, low at the front, high at the back; the card at the focus is drawn crisp and bright and the cards either side go soft with an echoed outline.
controls: focus: shade and position. The crisp bright outline and its detailed wave top step from card to card along the stack (front card at 100 Hz, back card at 8 kHz); five card steps, about 180 px of travel.
tilt: scale. Each card's height scales with its band's gain, so the stack's silhouette tilts: at −6 dB/oct the front cards stand tall and the back ones sink, at +6 the reverse (heights 0.6× to 1.6×).
blur: position. Every out-of-focus card's top contour is echoed by a dark hairline lifted above it, and its own wave flattens; blur lifts the echo from 3 px to 24 px and irons the wave out.
mix: position. The spacing of the stack: at 0 the six cards collapse onto one plane (dry: no depth, nothing separated), at 100 they spread to 36 px apart diagonally.
variants.reference: library/toro-blocks/contact.png (depth, hidden-line black fills) and opxy/reference/README.md (DPRO-WAVE-style stack via patterns.md P4)
risks: Front cards hide most of the cards behind; only their tops and right edges show, so the focal card's detail is only visible in a strip ~36 px wide when it isn't the front card.
The echoed contours of six cards cross each other and read as a nest of wavy lines on the left at blur 40 %; at blur 100 it may turn into hatching.

Focus steps in six cards while the control has twenty positions; between octaves the bright card can't move, so focus needs a second cue (the crisp detail sliding across the card) or it reads as stepped.
Six stacked cards is at the 5–6 cap from P4.

variants.subject: A surveyed plot of square markers laid out frequency by time, where a vertical strip at the focus is surveyed sharp (bright solid markers, crisp hits) and the rest of the ground is smeared into even, hollow, mid-size markers.
controls: focus: position. The two strip boundary lines (1.5 px, past the neat line) and the solid bright markers between them slide across the plan, 100 Hz to 8 kHz, about 330 px.
tilt: scale. Marker size ramps across the plan from low to high frequency: at −6 the low side swells and the high side shrinks to 4 px, +6 the reverse (each marker 4–14 px).

blur: scale over time. Outside the strip each column's markers even out down the time axis: at 0 every column has the strip's crisp pattern (big at the three hits, tiny between), at 100 every row is the same mid size, the hits smeared away.
mix: count. A seeded scatter of markers outside the strip swaps between the dry look (the crisp pattern) and the wet look (smeared); mix sets how many have swapped, 0 to all 160.
variants.reference: library/toro-blocks/contact.png (P10: a field computed from the signal model) beside opxy/reference/field-and-figure.jpg (neat ground, one figure)
risks: At 1:1 it reads as a matrix of LEDs or graph paper: a regular grid of identical squares is close to the 'dashboard of meters' the subject gate rejects.

Tilt and blur both change marker size (one across frequency, one down time); two controls on the scale channel of the same parts breaks the one-channel-per-control rule unless blur moves to shape (stretching markers into streaks along time) instead.
Size differences inside the haze are small at the default; the field looks uniform outside the strip, which is right for the sound but dull.
192 markers is fine for the node budget, but tilt and blur each resize nearly all of them: a turn redraws ~160 nodes, well past ~20 per frame while easing.

variants.subject: The sound's texture cut through like a patent section, a block of square cells frequency by time in which the focal band stays as crisp solid cells on the hits and everything outside is cross-hatched cut material smeared into long runs.
controls: focus: position. The column pair that stays solid (bright, hits only) moves across the block, 100 Hz to 8 kHz, about 400 px; the hatching closes behind it.
tilt: count. The density of hatched cells ramps across the block: at −6 the low side fills and the high side empties, at +6 the reverse; about 40 cells change sides over the range.
blur: run length. Outside the band, hatched cells join into longer vertical runs (time smeared): at 0 they're single cells on the hit rows like the band, at 100 they run most of the block's height.
mix: count, second look. A seeded scatter of out-of-band cells keeps the dry look (a solid mid-grey cell on the hit rows, no hatching) instead of the cut look; mix 0 is all dry, 100 all hatched.
variants.reference: opxy/reference/README.md (stock dissolve engine, the cell-field approach) beside library/theseus-tower/contact.png (line-drawing restraint)
risks: Hatching is static art (hundreds of 1 px ribbons) and can't be swapped by palette, so each cell needs a pre-hatched variant to show or hide: two nodes per cell, 320 nodes, needs sdk 1.8 and is heavy.
P15 is for noise-like sounds; tilt processes whatever is sent to it, so this only fits by saying the drawing is the effect's texture, not the source. Gate 0 has to be argued.
Hatched regions at 5 px pitch look like 'disabled' stipple from desktop UIs; a patent reader sees cut material, a player may see greyed-out.
Tilt and mix are both counts on the same cells; they differ by which look (hatched vs dry solid) and where (gradient vs scatter), which may not be enough to tell them apart.

variants.subject: A tilt-shift miniature: the spectrum built as a row of thin fins on a model base, with an upright glass plane of focus standing across it that captures the fins inside its depth of field as solid and leaves the rest hollow and doubled.
controls: focus: position. The plane of focus and its two depth-of-field lines on the base slide along the row, 100 Hz to 8 kHz, about 260 px of screen travel; fins entering it turn solid, fins leaving it go hollow.
tilt: shape. The base tips: fin heights ramp along the row about the plane of focus, so at −6 the near end towers and the far end sinks to stubs, at +6 the reverse (each fin 8–56 px).
blur: position. Each fin outside the depth of field casts a hollow ghost of itself set back into the base; blur pushes the ghost from 0 to ~14 px back, further for fins further from focus.
mix: position. No twin in the optics; a plain scale along the base's front edge (octave ticks, a 1.5 px bar) fills from 0 to the full length.
variants.reference: library/meikyu-capture/README.md (P13: the machine's rule drawn as a physical thing) beside library/toro-blocks/contact.png (hidden-line boxes)
variants.stretch: Why this machine might be the exception: P13 asks for the machine's own rule drawn as a physical thing with the same shape, and tilt's rule is literally an optical one (a plane of focus that keeps a band sharp and lets the rest go soft). The capture is the depth of field: what's inside it is sharp. Where it doesn't fit: P13 is a player/function pattern built on items being let through to play; here nothing is let through, only sharpened, and two of the four controls (tilt, mix) have no twin in the optics, so half the screen is scenery.
risks: Honest verdict on the stretch: it fits for focus and blur, and doesn't for tilt (a sloped base is a stand-in) or mix (a ruler in the corner, which P13 itself warns looks bolted on).
Twenty-two fins in a row read as a bookshelf or dominoes before they read as a spectrum; the glass plane is the only cue that this is about focus.
The camera is dimetric (24°/30°), not true isometric, to fit 300 px of row into a 200 px body; a strict 30° row would need ~170 px of drop.
Close to toro's hidden-line block field in look; the composition (one row, one plane) has to keep it from reading as a copy.
